items.stem: What is recursion?
options: When a function returns two values
When a loop runs forever
When a subroutine calls itself
When two programs share data
items.answer: When a subroutine calls itself
items.markingKey: It must have a base case and a general case that moves towards it.

items.stem: Explain why a recursive subroutine must have a base case.
items.answer: Without it the subroutine keeps calling itself; each call adds a stack frame, so memory runs out (stack overflow) and the program crashes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why recursion can use more memory than iteration.
items.answer: Every recursive call pushes a new stack frame (return address, parameters, locals) that remains until the call returns; a loop reuses the same variables.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem:
Study the recursive function:
FUNCTION SumDigits(Value : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Value < 10 THEN
        RETURN Value
    ELSE
        RETURN (Value MOD 10) + SumDigits(Value DIV 10)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
Identify the base case and the general case, and state how many times the function is called (including the first call) when SumDigits(206) is evaluated.
items.answer: Base case: IF Value < 10 THEN RETURN Value; general case: RETURN (Value MOD 10) + SumDigits(Value DIV 10); 3 calls
items.markingKey: base case (1); general case (1); 3 calls (1) [3]

ENDFUNCTION
Identify the base case and the general case, and state how many times the function is called (including the first call) when Mystery(37, 8) is evaluated.
items.answer: Base case: IF A < B THEN RETURN A; general case: RETURN Mystery(A - B, B); 5 calls
items.markingKey: base case (1); general case (1); 5 calls (1) [3]

items.stem:

    ENDIF

items.answer: (a) 2 (b) Advantage: shorter, clearer code for naturally recursive problems (trees). Disadvantage: more memory; risk of stack overflow; slower due to call overheads.

items.stem: A programmer at Nova Telecom in Lisbon has written several recursive functions. (a) Describe the features that every recursive subroutine must have. (b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of recursion compared with iteration.
items.answer: (a) A base case that stops the recursion; a general case that calls itself; each call moves closer to the base case. (b) Advantage: shorter, clearer code for naturally recursive problems (trees). Disadvantage: more memory; risk of stack overflow; slower due to call overheads.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per point [3] (b) 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: What is the base case of a recursive subroutine?
options: The largest possible input
The recursive call
The first line of the subroutine
The condition under which the subroutine returns without calling itself
items.answer: The condition under which the subroutine returns without calling itself
items.markingKey: It stops the recursion.

items.stem: What is the general case of a recursive subroutine?
options: The part where the subroutine calls itself with a value closer to the base case
The parameter list
The part that stops the recursion
The return type
items.answer: The part where the subroutine calls itself with a value closer to the base case
items.markingKey: e.g. RETURN N * Factorial(N - 1).

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

items.stem:
The recursive function is called with Countdown(13).
FUNCTION Countdown(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF N = 0 THEN
        RETURN 0
    ELSE
        RETURN N + Countdown(N - 2)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
Explain what happens and suggest a correction.
items.answer: N decreases by 2, so for an odd starting value N skips 0 and becomes negative; the base case is never reached and the stack overflows. Fix: IF N <= 0 THEN.
items.markingKey: 1 mark base case never reached; 1 mark stack overflow; 1 mark correction [3]

items.stem:
Rewrite this recursive function as an iterative function that gives the same result.
FUNCTION SumTo(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF N = 0 THEN
        RETURN 0
    ELSE
        RETURN N + SumTo(N - 1)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.answer:
FUNCTION SumTo(N : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    Total ← 0
    FOR i ← 1 TO N
        Total ← Total + i
    NEXT i
    RETURN Total
ENDFUNCTION
items.markingKey: 1 mark loop structure; 1 mark correct initialisation; 1 mark correct update; 1 mark return [4]

items.stem:
Study the function:
FUNCTION AddDigits(Num : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER

        RETURN Num
    ELSE
        RETURN (Num MOD 10) + AddDigits(Num DIV 10)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
AddDigits(530) is evaluated. Describe the contents of the call stack when the base case is reached (top of stack last), and explain how the final result is produced.
items.answer: Frames (bottom to top): AddDigits(530), AddDigits(53), AddDigits(5); each holds return address, parameter(s) and space for local values. The base case returns, then each frame is popped in turn and its return value used by the caller: AddDigits(5) = 5 → AddDigits(53) = 8 → AddDigits(530) = 8; result 8.

items.answer: Frames (bottom to top): AddDigits(971), AddDigits(97), AddDigits(9); each holds return address, parameter(s) and space for local values.
